newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold closes marginally firmer in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: HK gold closes marginally firmer in quiet trade.

text.p: Gold closed marginally firmer in Hong Kong on Monday after trading within a 30 U.S. cent range all day in an extremely quiet session due to the market holiday in Japan, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$382.40/90 an ounce against New York's US$382.20/70 close on Friday.

"The local market has been very quiet, with a small amount of short-covering interest," said a dealer at an international metals house. "The gold market was showing little reaction to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) discussions on Friday."
The IMF on Friday put off a decision on a proposal to sell a small amount of its gold to help the world's poorest nations.
Gold remains stuck in a range and is likely to continue thus with resistance at US$385 and support at US$380, traders said.
Local gold ended HK$1 higher at HK$3,525 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at -6 on Monday.
